subject: Your Model is Already Obsolete: Making Model Swaps a Non-Event
body:
Hello First Name,

Hope you're having a great week! Our latest 🦄 ai that works session tackled a really important topic: "Your Model is Already Obsolete: Making Model Swaps a Non-Event."

You can find the full recording, code, and diagrams from the session right here on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We dove deep into how to build solid evaluation systems that make swapping out old models for new ones much smoother. Here are the key takeaways:

*   **Know Your 'Good Enough':** Before anything else, clearly define what success looks like for your workflow. Think about accuracy, cost, and latency. This sets the bar for any new model you bring in.
*   **Use Diffing for Smarter Evals:** Don't hand-label every single test case. Instead, compare the outputs of your current model against the new candidate. Focus your manual review only on the cases where they differ. This is a super efficient way to build and refine your golden dataset.
*   **Create a Flexible Eval System:** Set up a system that lets you easily swap models in and out. You should also be able to quickly adjust evaluation settings, like the maximum acceptable accuracy drop or latency tolerance, to rapidly test new models.

If there's one key takeaway from this session, it's this: Model deprecations are just a fact of life in AI. Building systems that anticipate these changes and make model upgrades a routine, non-event is absolutely crucial for avoiding those stressful, last-minute emergencies.

Got questions? Just reply to this email or hop over to our Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We read every single message! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
